summary: Preserve vertex correspondence from Blender shape keys through exported primitive splits and runtime morph attributes.
objective: Every target delta addresses the intended base vertex and survives the declared mesh processing and runtime representation.
applies_when: A mesh with shape keys or morph targets passes through export, vertex processing, simplification or runtime geometry replacement.
intent_signals: morph target count matches but vertices are scrambled
LOD cannot reuse face expression deltas
example_prompts: Export facial shape keys without scrambling vertices at UV seams.
Rebuild a simplified creature mesh with compatible morph targets.
negative_signals: copy high resolution morph deltas into decimated geometry
not_for: Expression timing, emotion design or mixer channel arbitration.
Topology-changing remeshing represented as a fixed-vertex morph.

principles: Equal counts are necessary for the exported attribute arrays but do not prove matching vertex order or meaning. Maintain the base-to-target correspondence through every reorder, seam split and optimization.

Blender shape keys share the object topology. Shared edits after key creation can be possible, but a stable-topology authoring checkpoint makes correspondence reviewable. Each derived LOD needs its own compatible target set or an explicit reduced-expression policy.
Separate absolute target coordinates from additive deltas. The runtime relative flag and loader result must match the representation; a name dictionary is semantic metadata, not geometric proof.
implementation: In Blender, settle base topology before detailed keys where practical. Record Basis/reference relationships, target order and representative isolated and combined shapes; evaluate exported output after modifiers and seam splits.

Inspect each exported primitive: target order/count, matching base semantic, accessor counts, compatible attribute types and intended vertex correspondence. A reordered base requires the same mapping on every relevant target stream; recompute or transfer targets when the topology actually changes.

For Three.js, inspect loaded morphAttributes and morphTargetsRelative before modifying weights. Do not overwrite rendered morph attribute data in place when the installed API requires a new geometry; dispose only resources owned by the replacement operation.

Verify names/index mapping separately, then compare a few marked vertices and asymmetric target shapes at base, isolated and permitted combined weights. Preserve material and UV seams as intended rather than blindly welding them.
observable_checks: A one-vertex or asymmetric marker target moves the intended feature after export and any optimization; a deliberate index permutation is rejected even if counts match.
All primitives agree on target order and count, while each target accessor matches its own base primitive count.
Base and approved combined poses retain intended normals, seams and attachments; reset restores the declared base/default weights.

creative_affordances: Use coarse expressive targets on distant levels when that is the declared design.
Combine sculpted morphs with skeletal movement under explicit channel ownership.
known_limits: No authoring, export, deformation or rendered fixture ran.
Documented glTF attribute options do not guarantee support by every loader or renderer revision.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5 describes shape keys as positions for all vertices on shared object topology. It allows shared vertex additions/deletions after key creation while recommending that shape keys be created once topology is finished or stable.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 manual; no claim that arbitrary remeshing preserves expressive correspondence.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 morph target attributes are deltas requiring a matching base attribute. All primitives of a mesh have the same target count and order, and target accessors have the same count as the original primitive accessors.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0 section 3.7.2.2; count/order checks do not prove correct semantic vertex correspondence.

source_refs.locator: 3.7.2.2 Morph Targets: target deltas, base attributes, target order and accessor counts

claims.statement: Current Three.js BufferGeometry documents morphAttributes and states that rendered morph attribute data cannot be changed without disposing and creating a new geometry; morphTargetsRelative selects relative offsets instead of absolute positions/normals.
claims.scope: Live documentation accessed 2026-09-08; weight playback and owned resource cleanup are separate from attribute replacement.
